## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah Altmann [10. Februar 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.98
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.98
- Datum: 10.2.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 7 Scans

pages.transcription:
Newyork, 10. II. 41

Dear Hanna,
I am in a hurry, having to leave for
Newhaven in a few minutes where I am flat-
hunting. I want to tell you that I went to see
Eva yesterday in her new home and found her
very satisfied, and in my opinion already more at
home than she ever was at Salmon's. She likes the
new school, there are very nice children at Schaeffer's
as far as I saw them yesterday. I spent two hours
there and liked it very much and Eva was her old
self, gay, affectionate and lively. For the moment
there are no girls in her exact age at Amity Hall,
but just yesterday a girl of 14 arrived and more are
in prospect. What Eva is not yet quite used to,
she says, is the noise and being so much outdoors.
But the weather was particularly bad the last days
and as she is her father's daughter I can under-
stand that it will take her a little time to get
to like outdoor sports. But everything else she
likes very much.
I have to leave now, so only best love
and thanks for your letter N°2 to Newyork of Jan 22nd.
Yours, Lotte
Dear Hannah, before all, you must not worry about Eva. We have
the best impression of Mrs Schaeffer's house, especially when this horrid
cold weather will be over and the verandahs, the garden to be used
so that the children there will more dispersed. Now they are in the eve-
ning all together in one big hall and of all ages, but these days of
bitter frost will pass soon and she has already made many friends. Mrs Schaeffer
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf zwei Seiten (Vorderseite). Die letzten Zeilen sind am unteren Rand quer geschrieben.

pages.transcription:
so that you can give it to my lawyer Mr. Wilenor[?]. You cannot imagine
how through this travelling from Uruguay to Brazil and the States all my
correspondence is in disorder, I hear and have nothing and it will be diffi-
cult to keep order. We feel physically all right, but imagine how we hate
this continual packing, how boring it is to travel with all manuscripts and
notes and different drafts from hotel to hotel, never to have space and to
have at the same time a house at home, where I could work quickly - poor
Lotte does not know where to correct the different copies, the bed, the floor
all is always overflooded with typewritten paper. I would be glad could we
find at Newhaven, where the Yale University gives me all facilities a flat
for two or three month to finish my book!! But there are no factories
and all flats taken and I will not stay at Newyork, which is rather ex-
pensive and where I have no quiet moment. I asked here my friend at
the consulate, he tells me that there are now no possibilities of passage
and the clipper is taken for months; so we will probably return to Rio
in the summer. But who can make plans! Who can say "I will", "I intend"
- one must be satisfied to live and I want all my will-power to
continue working in midst of this turmoil.
About your friend Forschauer nothing will astonish
me. He came and told that he is citizen (that surely is not true / has
visit cards (for bluffing) as "Chairman of Associated Correspondents"
and perhaps he will catch some innocent people by this blunder. I be-
lieve he will soon leave Brazil as now visas for immigrants are rarely
available for all who are out of Europe; the quota became suddenly opened
as all those who has the numbers in Europe are unable to travel; all those
who are already in Cuba, Mexico or South America can get them easily
and if Eva would come to Cuba all would be easy. I spoke with
his daughter, he wish both to have him over and are both afraid of the
voyage in this moment. I hope you will go soon to Bath with Lartor[?],
I would prefer to know you there for a rest after the strenuous weeks.
And please, be sure, that Eva is in best care. To be traveller yesterday to see her
today she is in Newhaven - how wonderful must it be to sit quietly
a few weeks in the same place! Yours Stefan Zweig
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf der zweiten Seite des Bogens. Am linken Rand befindet sich ein vertikal geschriebener Zusatz.

pages.transcription:
is excellent and very careful, but now she phoned me, that she wants like
to bring Eva (without any actual pain) to the dentist, because she has not
been looked over since more than half a year. You see by this little detail
that she thinks on everything and I believe that Eva by being mixed with
children of different age (till to 14 / different languages, religions and so on
will get beyond the school-instruction a good deal of life-experience. She
has an easy way to adapt herself and we hope that the school will accept
her without any fee. It seems to be a very interesting school and your
daughter has to do her first essays in art, she painted a view of Bath
and has to try modelling and they give lectures and play theatre - you
must understand that all is not very serious and mixes fun with in-
struction in a quite new way. As on the other hand she has continental
education at Mrs Schaeffer at home, she will have in my opinion very
great advantages and she will have to tell you a lot when we meet again.
Now I have to ask you a favour. I do not like very much to
worry you as I know that every little way and walk is no pleasure now.
When we left we forgot to take with us our birth-certificates and
our marriage certificate; we could manage to get the different visas by
protection without that, but in the long run - who could believe that
we could not return in December? - it would be better to have them. They
are in the library in the documents safe and you will easily find them
but it would be better before to send them to let make a simple photography
the birth-certificates (the other we have in two copies) and perhaps let
certify the copies by a notary (Ingram or other). We do not want them
for a special purpose, but we may want them; it was a great mistake
of ours not to have these documents with us, but who could think of all
this formalism which rules now everywhere!! It is a harry at all!
I wrote to Cassels to send the author-copy of my last
book to Bath and I hope he will do it. By the way I would ask you
to make regularly notes of all that came in during my absence
on literary income (not income from investments, this will be done
directly by the bank) as in April I have to have it ready for the person
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf der dritten Seite des Bogens.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der kursiven Handschrift von Stefan Zweig. Einige wenige Eigennamen sind aufgrund der Handschrift leicht unsicher, aber im Kontext gut interpretierbar.
